title: Coffee in a city
prompt: Estimate how many cups of coffee are bought in a city of 1 million people in a year.
approach: Start with the population: 1,000,000 people.
Not everyone drinks coffee. Assume 60% do, which is 600,000 drinkers.
Assume the average drinker buys half a cup a day outside the home (most coffee is made at home): 300,000 cups a day.
Multiply by 365 days to get about 110 million cups a year.

title: Dentists in a city
prompt: Estimate how many dentists a city of 500,000 people needs.
approach: Demand: 500,000 people each visit a dentist about twice a year, which is 1,000,000 visits.
Supply per dentist: about 8 patients a day, for about 200 working days, which is 1,600 visits a year.
Divide demand by supply: 1,000,000 / 1,600 is about 625 dentists.

title: A pizza shop's revenue
prompt: Estimate the annual revenue of a busy takeaway pizza shop.
approach: Think in orders: a busy shop might take about 120 orders a day.
Assume an average order of $25 (a couple of pizzas and a side).
Assume it trades about 350 days a year.
120 x $25 x 350 is about $1 million a year.

title: Piano tuners in a metro area
prompt: Estimate how many piano tuners work in a metropolitan area of 2 million people.
approach: Households: 2,000,000 people at 2.5 per household is 800,000 households.
Pianos: assume 1 household in 50 owns a piano, so 16,000 pianos.
Demand: each piano is tuned about once a year, so 16,000 tunings.
Supply per tuner: about 4 tunings a day for 200 days is 800 a year.
16,000 / 800 is about 20 piano tuners.

title: Daily subway trips
prompt: Estimate how many commuter trips are made on a city's subway on a weekday. The city has 3 million people.
approach: Workers: about 40% of 3 million people are commuting workers, which is 1.2 million.
Assume 25% of them commute by subway: 300,000 people.
Each makes two trips a day (there and back): 600,000 commuter trips.
Non-commuting trips would add to this, so treat 600,000 as a floor.

title: Smartphones sold in a year
prompt: Estimate how many smartphones are sold each year in a country of 60 million people.
approach: Owners: assume 80% of the population has a smartphone, which is 48 million.
People replace a phone about every 3 years, so one third of owners buy each year.
48 million / 3 is about 16 million phones a year (ignoring first-time buyers).

title: Taxis in a city
prompt: Estimate how many taxis a city of 2 million people needs.
approach: Demand: assume 1 person in 20 takes a taxi on a given day, which is 100,000 trips.
Supply: a taxi completes about 25 trips a day.
100,000 / 25 is about 4,000 taxis (more to cover peaks and downtime).

title: Gym membership revenue
prompt: Estimate the yearly revenue from gym memberships in a city of 1 million people.
approach: Adults: about 70% of the population is adult, which is 700,000.
Members: assume 15% of adults hold a gym membership, which is 105,000.
Fee: assume $40 a month, which is $480 a year.
105,000 x $480 is about $50 million a year.

title: Weddings in a year
prompt: Estimate how many weddings take place each year in a country of 60 million people.
approach: People per year of age: 60 million spread over about 80 years of life is about 750,000.
Assume 70% of people marry at some point: about 525,000 people marry per age cohort.
Each wedding involves two people, so about 262,500 weddings a year.

title: Milk drunk in a city
prompt: Estimate how many litres of milk a city of 1 million people drinks in a day.
approach: Start per person: a glass of milk is about a quarter of a litre.
Averaged across everyone (many people drink none, some drink more), assume about 0.25 litres a day.
1,000,000 x 0.25 is about 250,000 litres a day.

title: Pharmacies in a city
prompt: Estimate how many pharmacies a city of 600,000 people supports.
approach: Use a rule of thumb for how many people it takes to keep one pharmacy busy: about 3,000.
600,000 / 3,000 is about 200 pharmacies.
Sense-check: that is about one for every few streets, which feels right for a city.

title: Sunscreen sales
prompt: Estimate how many bottles of sunscreen are sold each year in a country of 40 million people.
approach: Users: assume about half the population uses sunscreen in a year, which is 20 million.
Each user buys about 1.5 bottles a year.
20 million x 1.5 is about 30 million bottles a year.
